name: Jabal
title: Father of Nomadic Life
summary: Jabal was the son of Lamech and Adah, and he is regarded as the ancestor of those who live in tents and keep livestock. He is mentioned in Genesis as one of the early cultural pioneers in the lineage of Cain, representing the beginning of nomadic shepherding as a way of life.
relatedPersons: Lamech (son of Methuselah, descendant of Cain)

keyEvents.title: The Birth and Lineage of Jabal
keyEvents.description: Jabal was born as the son of Lamech and Adah, in the seventh generation from Adam through the line of Cain.

keyEvents.title: Ancestor of Tent-dwellers and Livestock Keepers
keyEvents.description: Jabal became the father of all who live in tents and keep livestock, thus establishing the nomadic shepherd lifestyle as an organized way of life.

keyEvents.title: Part of Cain's cultural development
keyEvents.description: Jabal was part of the cultural development in Cain's lineage, where his brothers Jubal and Tubal-Cain contributed music and metalworking.

keyEvents.title: Lamech's family and descendants
keyEvents.description: Jabal's father Lamech was the first to take two wives, Adah and Zillah, and through his sons he became the source of several cultural and technological advances in early human civilization.
